headline: High: Airflow and Prefect both have broad network egress, creating default data-exfiltration and workflow-conflict risk; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, Airflow can call APIs and Prefect also calls APIs, so if an operator bridges them through files or workflow metadata, one agent’s outputs could be treated as instructions. This is an inferred pathway, not directly documented.
conditions: IF the operator connects Airflow task outputs into Prefect task inputs via files, queues, or copied text
IF either agent is configured to parse the other’s output as instructions
mitigations: Keep outputs as structured data, not free text
Add an explicit instruction/content separator in handoffs
Review any copied task logs before reuse
Disable automatic ingestion of upstream text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress and Prefect also has broad network egress, so either can transmit workflow metadata or embedded file contents if connected to sensitive inputs. The profiles do not show secrets handling or shared workspace, so this is not high, but default egress makes leakage plausible in ordinary deployments.
conditions: IF either agent receives sensitive workflow metadata or file contents
IF outbound destinations are not allowlisted
mitigations: Restrict outbound network destinations
Strip secrets from workflow metadata
Use separate service accounts
Turn on redaction for logs and task payloads
requires-engineering: isolate sensitive pipelines from internet-reachable workers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents are workflow orchestrators with broad network egress, so they can compete over the same mutable external resources even though filesystem or git write access is not documented. The overlap is enough to create coordination conflicts on shared APIs or workflow state, but the evidence does not support high severity because unrestricted same-directory writes are not shown.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external workflow state or API resource
IF no locking or ownership convention exists
mitigations: Assign disjoint resource namespaces
Add optimistic-lock retries
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Audit shared API targets for collisions
requires-engineering: implement distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow and Prefect are both automation systems, so one can feed outputs into the other and propagate mistakes if the downstream flow trusts upstream results. There is no evidence of built-in verification between them, but the pairwise interaction is plausible in default orchestration setups, making cascading errors a realistic medium risk.
conditions: IF Airflow task outputs are consumed by Prefect flows without validation
IF downstream tasks act on upstream-generated parameters
mitigations: Add schema validation at handoff points
Require human review for destructive steps
Log and compare upstream vs downstream inputs
Use checksum or signature checks on artifacts
requires-engineering: add explicit verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Only Prefect explicitly lists workflow metadata as a touched data class, while Airflow’s profile does not name regulated data classes or residency constraints. With no documented mismatch in retention, residency, or certifications, compliance risk is limited to ordinary metadata handling rather than a clear breach pathway.
conditions: IF workflow metadata contains regulated identifiers
IF retention or residency policies differ in the deployment
mitigations: Classify workflow metadata before sharing
Minimize logged identifiers
Set a common retention policy
Review residency requirements for any regulated fields
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both systems
